name: Anjan Prasad
homeBlurb: Ten-plus years on the hiring side of the table â€” as interviewer, consultant and founder. Anjan built Fundamental after watching hundreds of capable graduates lose offers for skills no one had ever shown them.
shortBio: 10+ years on the hiring side. Building the institute he wishes existed.
aboutParagraphs: For over a decade, I've been on the other side of the hiring table â€” interviewing candidates, advising businesses and building as a founder.
One interview stayed with me. A bright MBA graduate could explain every marketing framework, but struggled when I asked her to plan a month of marketing for a cafÃ©.
It wasn't a question of intelligence or effort. It was the gap between knowing the theory and knowing how to apply it.
I realised that capable graduates don't just need more information. They need the opportunity to practise, make decisions, learn from feedback and build skills they can take into a real job.
That's why I built Fundamental: practitioner-led learning where the focus isn't just on what you know, but on what you can actually do.

Over the years, I've also taught as visiting faculty at IMT Ghaziabad, BML Munjal University and IIFT â€” and the same pattern showed up in every classroom. Students learn fastest when they work on something real, and someone from the industry reviews it honestly.

So that's how we run things here. Small batches. Live sessions. A real brief every week, with feedback you can act on. And one simple promise: we'll always tell you the truth about your work â€” because the industry will, too.

title: Why 51% of graduates can't get hired â€” and what to do about it
excerpt: The employability gap isn't about effort. It's about being taught the subject instead of the job. Here's how to close it in 90 days.

children.text: Every year, lakhs of graduates leave college with a degree in one hand and a resume nobody calls back in the other. The NASSCOM number that gets quoted â€” roughly half of graduates unemployable in their field â€” is not a comment on talent. It is a comment on what colleges optimise for.

Colleges teach the subject: definitions, theories, end-of-chapter questions. Companies hire for the job: can you run the campaign, read the funnel, write the brief, present the work. These are different skills, and the gap between them is exactly the gap an interview exposes.

The fix is not another recorded course. It is reps â€” real briefs, reviewed by someone from the hiring side, until the work is good enough to show a panel. That is the entire design philosophy behind Fundamental's 50 live hours.

title: What hiring managers actually ask in a marketing interview
excerpt: After a decade on the hiring side of the table, these are the five questions that separate offers from rejections.

children.text: Interviewers rarely ask you to define the 4 Ps. They ask what you would do with a shrinking budget, a campaign that stopped converting, a founder who wants virality by Friday.

The pattern behind every good answer is the same: a real example, a number, and a decision you can defend. Candidates who have only consumed content have none of the three. Candidates who have shipped work â€” even training work on live accounts â€” have all of them.
This is why every week of the program ends in a brief, and why the capstone is a campaign you can walk a panel through end to end.

title: Online vs offline: which batch actually fits your week?
excerpt: Same curriculum, same mentors, two very different rhythms. A practical guide to choosing your mode.

children.text: The online batch runs Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 8:30 to 10 PM â€” focused evening sessions after your workday ends. It suits students and working professionals alike.

The offline batch runs Saturday and Sunday afternoons, 2 to 4 PM, at the Hinjewadi studio. In-person sessions, mock interviews, and the energy of a room. It is built for people who want their weekdays untouched.
Whichever you pick, the curriculum, mentoring, certificate and internship eligibility are identical. Choose the rhythm you can actually sustain for 3 months.
